content.text:
I now have everything needed. Here's the full research report.

## 1. Asset Manager — API surface for decoded pixel data

**No decoder is wired into `packages/assets` itself — it's a pure DI-interface layer.**

- `packages/assets/src/metadata.ts:46-48` — `IMetadataExtractor.extract(data, type, mimeType): Promise<IAssetMetadata>` is the only decode-adjacent interface. `IImageMetadata`/`IVideoMetadata` (`metadata.ts:4-17`) carry `width`/`height` (Video also `fps`, `durationTicks`, `hasAudio`) — but this is a **one-shot metadata read at import time**, not a queryable decoded-frame API.
- `packages/assets/src/thumbnail-generator.ts:11-13` — `IThumbnailGenerator.generate(data, type, mimeType): Promise<Uint8Array | undefined>` — also one-shot, produces a JPEG thumbnail, not usable as a live texture source.
- **Real decoders exist only at the app layer**, not in `packages/assets`:
  - `apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/metadata-extractor.ts:22-33` — `readImageMetadata` uses `createImageBitmap(new Blob(...))`.
  - `apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/metadata-extractor.ts:35-63` — `readVideoMetadata` uses a `document.createElement("video")` + `onloadedmetadata`, hardcodes `ASSET_METADATA_FPS = 30` (`metadata-extractor.ts:19`), and always reports `hasAudio: true` (no real demux, `metadata-extractor.ts:47-50`).
  - `apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/thumbnail-generator.ts:64-77` — image thumbnail via `createImageBitmap` + `canvas.drawImage`.
  - `apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/thumbnail-generator.ts:79-113` — video thumbnail via `<video>` + seek + `canvas.drawImage(video, ...)` (`drawToThumbnailCanvas`, line 44-62, takes a `CanvasImageSource`).
  - **No WebCodecs `VideoDecoder`/`VideoFrame` anywhere in `src/`** (only mentioned in doc comments as aspirational — `color-space.ts:30`, `frame-cache.ts:58`).
- **`AssetCatalog`/`IAssetCatalogEntry` does NOT expose width/height.** `packages/assets/src/asset-catalog.ts:10-21` — fields are `id, name, type, mimeType, sizeBytes, durationTicks, contentHash, tags, createdAt`. Width/height from `IAssetMetadata` (extracted at import) is **used and discarded** — only `durationTicks` (line 93-96 of `import-pipeline.ts`) survives into the catalog entry. There is currently no persisted, queryable intrinsic-dimension field for an asset.
- `packages/assets/src/dependency-graph.ts` — `AssetDependencyGraph` only tracks reference-id ↔ assetId edges (`registerReference`/`getReferences`/`getAssetFor`, lines 28-52); no pixel data.
- `AssetManager` (`packages/assets/src/asset-manager.ts:30-98`) exposes `import`, `get`, `list`, `getThumbnail` (line 58, thumbnail only, tick fixed to `toTick(0)`), `delete`, `registerReference`/`unregisterReference`, `listUnused`. **There is no `getBytes`/`getBlob`/`getDecodedFrame` method on `AssetManager` at all.**

## 2. Layer → Asset linkage

- `packages/shared/src/layer.ts:31-35` — `IVideoLayer extends ILayerBase { type: LayerType.Video; assetId: AssetId; playbackRate: number }`
- `packages/shared/src/layer.ts:37-41` — `IImageLayer extends ILayerBase { type: LayerType.Image; assetId: AssetId; fitMode: "contain"|"cover"|"fill"|"none" }`
- `packages/shared/src/layer.ts:43-47` — `IAudioLayer` also has `assetId: AssetId` (+ `volume`)
- `packages/shared/src/layer.ts:58-61` — `IStickerLayer` also has `assetId: AssetId`
- `ITextLayer`/`IShapeLayer`/`IGroupLayer` have no `assetId` (text/shape/group are non-asset-backed).
- `packages/layer/src/layer-factory.ts:49,56-57` / `:63,70-71` / `:111,117-118` — factory functions (`createVideoLayer`, `createImageLayer`, `createStickerLayer`) take `assetId` as required input and copy it straight onto the layer.
- **Important gap**: `IFrameStateLayer`/`ISceneGraphNode` (built by `frame-state-builder.ts`/`scene-graph.ts`) do **not** carry `assetId` at all — they only forward `properties: Record<string, unknown>` from `getLayerPropertyValue`. Currently `assetId` is not one of the "animatable properties" iterated in `frame-state-builder.ts:70-82`, so it never makes it into `properties`. Any texture-wiring plan needs to either add `assetId` to `IFrameStateLayer`/`ISceneGraphNode` directly, or ensure it flows through `properties`.

## 3. Storage/VFS call path for raw bytes

Trace from an `assetId` down to bytes:

1. `AssetCatalog.get(assetId)` → `packages/assets/src/asset-catalog.ts:48-50` → returns `IAssetCatalogEntry` (has `contentHash`).
2. `contentHash` → `AssetBlobStore.get(hash)` → `packages/storage/src/asset-blob-store.ts:24-26` → `this.vfs.read(this.pathFor(hash))` where `pathFor` = `` `assets/${hash}` `` (line 36-38).
3. `IVFS` = `IStorageAdapter` (`packages/storage/src/vfs.ts:9`, `storage-adapter.ts:7-14`) → `read(path): Promise<Uint8Array | undefined>`, backed by `StorageEngine` routing IndexedDB/OPFS per path prefix (not read in depth here, but `storage-engine.ts` is the router).
4. **Wiring gap**: `AssetManager` (`asset-manager.ts`) holds `options.blobStore` privately (`IAssetManagerOptions.blobStore`, line 12) but never exposes a `getBytes(assetId)` passthrough. `AssetEditorService` (`apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/services/asset-editor-service.ts`) only forwards `import/list/listUnused/getThumbnail/delete` — no raw-bytes accessor either.
5. `create-editor-kernel.ts:44-54` — constructs `blobStore = new AssetBlobStore(storageEngine)` and passes it into `AssetManager`'s options, but `blobStore` itself isn't retained on `EditorKernel` (only `storageEngine` and `assetManager` are public readonly fields, `editor-kernel.ts:43-44`). A render-glue module fetching raw bytes today would have to either (a) add a new `AssetManager.getBytes(assetId)` method that does catalog-lookup + blobStore.get, or (b) have `EditorKernel` retain and expose the `blobStore` separately.

So the realistic path to wire is: **rendering glue → new `AssetManager.getBytes(assetId): Promise<Uint8Array|undefined>` (catalog.get → blobStore.get) → decode via `createImageBitmap`/`<video>` element (same pattern as `metadata-extractor.ts`/`thumbnail-generator.ts`) → cache in a `TextureCache`/`DecodedFrameCache` → backend `drawImage`/texture upload.**

## 4. TextureCache — full read

`packages/rendering/src/texture-cache.ts` (52 lines, read in full):

```ts
export interface ITextureHandle {
  readonly key: string;
  readonly width: number;
  readonly height: number;
}

export interface ITextureCache {
  get(key: string): ITextureHandle | undefined;
  set(key: string, handle: ITextureHandle): void;
  has(key: string): boolean;
  delete(key: string): boolean;
  clear(): void;
  readonly size: number;
}

export class TextureCache implements ITextureCache { /* plain Map<string, ITextureHandle> wrapper */ }
```

- Backend-agnostic by design: `ITextureHandle` only carries `key/width/height` — no `GPUTexture`/`WebGLTexture`/`ImageBitmap` payload field. The doc comment (line 1) says the real payload type is "backend-specific" but **the interface as written has nowhere to put that payload** — any real implementation would need to extend `ITextureHandle` with e.g. `readonly data: GPUTexture | WebGLTexture | ImageBitmap` (not present today).
- **No eviction policy** — deliberate, per `docs/05-rendering-engine/gpu-memory.md:9-13` (no GPU memory budget number exists yet; CLAUDE.md "Known hard risks" #6 explicitly says don't build LRU until a real ceiling exists).
- **Nothing in the codebase instantiates `TextureCache`** — confirmed via grep, zero references outside `texture-cache.ts`/`texture-cache.test.ts`. Not wired into `RenderingEngine`, `rendering-engine.ts`, or any backend's constructor/`init`.
- Compare `packages/rendering/src/frame-cache.ts:14-54` — `DecodedFrameCache<TFrame>` (generic, JS-heap, LRU with count-based eviction, keyed by `(assetId, tick)`) — this one **is** eviction-capable and is the natural home for decoded `ImageBitmap`/`VideoFrame` objects, separate from `TextureCache` (GPU-side). Also unused anywhere currently.

## 5. Scene Graph / IRenderBackend — full shapes

- `packages/rendering/src/scene-graph.ts:20-28` — `ISceneGraphNode { layerId, type, transform, opacity, zIndex, bounds, properties: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> }`. Flat, no `assetId` field, no texture reference. `properties` is the only place asset info could ride through today (would need `frame-state-builder.ts` to populate it).
- `packages/rendering/src/render-backend.ts:17-22` — `IRenderBackend { kind, init(target: IRenderTargetSize): Promise<void>|void; drawFrame(sceneGraph: ISceneGraph): Promise<void>|void; dispose(): Promise<void>|void }`. Note `drawFrame` takes the **whole** `ISceneGraph`, not per-node — each backend internally loops `sortRenderQueue(sceneGraph.nodes)` and calls a private `drawNode`.
- Each backend's private `drawNode` signature (all currently ignore node type/properties and only use `transform`+`bounds`+`opacity`+`placeholderColor(node.layerId)`):

# Real texture content for Image/Video layers (Canvas panel)

## Context

The user reported that dropping an image/video onto the Canvas panel shows
only a small flat-colored square in the top-left corner instead of the
actual pixel content. Investigation confirmed this is not a wiring bug — no
render backend has ever drawn real pixel content. Every layer, regardless of
type, draws a `placeholderColor(layerId)` flat rect
(`packages/rendering/src/placeholder-color.ts`), and every layer's bounds
are hardcoded to a `200×200` placeholder box
(`apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/frame-state-builder.ts:24`) because no asset
dimension is tracked anywhere. This was an explicitly documented, deferred
gap (PLAN.md §15.2, §7), not previously implemented.

User chose the full-scope fix: wire real decoded image/video content into
**all four** render backends (WebGPU, WebGL2, Canvas2D, Software), and fix
layer bounds to reflect the asset's real dimensions instead of the
placeholder box. This is genuinely greenfield — no design doc or existing
decode-to-texture path exists to extend.

**Key existing patterns being reused, not reinvented:**
- Browser-only decode already exists twice for one-shot use:
  `apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/metadata-extractor.ts` (`createImageBitmap`
  for images, `<video>` + `onloadedmetadata` for video) and
  `thumbnail-generator.ts` (`<video>` + seek + `drawImage` to a canvas). The
  new resolver mirrors these same browser APIs, just kept alive instead of
  one-shot.
- `AssetManager` already composes `catalog.get` + `blobStore.get` internally
  for `delete()` — the new `getBytes` method follows the same shape.
- Every backend already hand-rolls a minimal DOM/GPU interface
  (`ICanvas2DContext`, `IWebGL2Context`, `IGPUDevice`) so tests can inject
  fakes — texture support extends these same interfaces rather than
  introducing a new abstraction.
- `packages/rendering` stays DOM-decode-free: `RenderingEngine` accepts an
  **injected** `ITextureSourceProvider`; the actual `createImageBitmap`/
  `<video>` decode logic lives in `apps/studio` (app layer owns DOM glue,
  same split as `metadata-extractor.ts`/`thumbnail-generator.ts` today).

**Explicitly out of scope** (flagged, not solved by this change):
- Text/Shape/Group layers keep `PLACEHOLDER_BOUNDS` — modeling their
  intrinsic size is a separate, already-flagged open item.
- Frame-exact video/tick sync — video playback drives the `<video>` element
  natively (play/pause in lockstep with the Playhead); scrubbing seeks it.
  This is an approximation, consistent with CLAUDE.md's already-open "Audio
  clock drift" hard risk (no resync strategy decided yet) — not solved here,
  not regressed either.
- GPU texture eviction/LRU — no GPU memory budget number exists yet
  (CLAUDE.md hard risk #6); texture caches in WebGL2/WebGPU backends stay
  unbounded for this pass, same accepted-risk posture as `TextureCache`.
- `packages/export`'s output — Export reuses the same `frame-state-builder`/
  Scene Graph, but wiring `ITextureSourceProvider` into the Export path is
  not in scope here (Export currently runs headless, no DOM); flag as a
  follow-up so preview/export parity isn't silently broken.

---

## Implementation stages

### 1. Assets: persist dimensions, expose raw bytes

- `packages/assets/src/asset-catalog.ts` — add
  `readonly width: number | undefined; readonly height: number | undefined;`
  to `IAssetCatalogEntry`, matching the existing `durationTicks: Tick | undefined`
  convention (not `?:`, per `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`). Undefined for
  Audio/Font/LUT and for assets imported before this change.
- `packages/assets/src/import-pipeline.ts` — currently extracts
  `IAssetMetadata` (which has `width`/`height` for Image/Video) and only
  keeps `durationTicks`. Also persist `width`/`height` onto the catalog
  entry when present.
- `packages/assets/src/asset-manager.ts` — add
  `getBytes(assetId): Promise<Uint8Array | undefined>`, composing
  `catalog.get(assetId)` → `blobStore.get(entry.contentHash)`, same
  composition style already used inline in `delete()`.

### 2. Shared + Rendering: texture types and plumbing

- `packages/shared/src/layer.ts` / `frame-state.ts` — add
  `assetId: AssetId | undefined` to `IFrameStateLayer` (mirrors `ILayer`'s
  existing `assetId` on Image/Video/Sticker/Audio layer types).
- New `packages/rendering/src/texture-source.ts`:
  ```ts
  export type ITextureSource =
    | { readonly kind: "image-source"; readonly source: CanvasImageSource; readonly width: number; readonly height: number }
    | { readonly kind: "raw-rgba"; readonly pixels: Uint8ClampedArray; readonly width: number; readonly height: number };

  export interface ITextureSourceProvider {
    resolve(assetId: AssetId): ITextureSource | undefined;
  }
  ```
  `CanvasImageSource` is an ambient `lib.dom` type — already safe to
  reference here since `tsconfig.base.json` includes `"DOM"` in `lib` (same
  ambient-type usage already present in `thumbnail-generator.ts`). Backends
  branch on `kind`: Canvas2D/WebGL2/WebGPU use `"image-source"`, Software
  uses `"raw-rgba"`; each falls back to the existing placeholder-color path
  if `texture` is absent or the wrong kind — the "explicit fallback path"
  rule from CLAUDE.md.
- `packages/rendering/src/scene-graph.ts` — add
  `readonly assetId: AssetId | undefined` and
  `readonly texture: ITextureSource | undefined` to `ISceneGraphNode`.
  `toSceneGraphNode`/`buildSceneGraph` take an optional
  `textureProvider?: ITextureSourceProvider` param and call
  `textureProvider?.resolve(layer.assetId)` when `layer.assetId` is set.
- `packages/rendering/src/rendering-engine.ts` — `RenderingEngine`
  constructor takes an optional `textureProvider?: ITextureSourceProvider`,
  passed through to `buildSceneGraph` in `renderFrame`.

### 3. Canvas2D backend — real `drawImage`

- `packages/rendering/src/canvas2d-backend.ts` — add
  `drawImage(image: CanvasImageSource, dx, dy, dw, dh): void` to
  `ICanvas2DContext`. In `drawNode`, if
  `node.texture?.kind === "image-source"`, call `ctx.drawImage(source, x, y, w, h)`

  instead of `fillStyle`+`fillRect`; otherwise keep the current placeholder
  path unchanged.
- Extend `packages/rendering/src/test-support/fake-canvas2d-context.ts` with
  a spy-able `drawImage`.

### 4. Software backend — raw RGBA sampling

- `packages/rendering/src/software-backend.ts` — in `drawNode`, if
  `node.texture?.kind === "raw-rgba"`, nearest-neighbor sample the source
  buffer per destination pixel (map dest pixel within `worldBounds` back to
  a normalized UV → source index) instead of the flat `r,g,b` from
  `placeholderColor`; keep `blendPixel`'s alpha compositing as-is. Falls
  back to placeholder color when no texture is present — this keeps the
  backend's "no canvas, no GPU, pure Node" purity intact, since the actual
  RGBA snapshot is always produced upstream in the browser-only resolver,
  never decoded by this backend itself.

### 5. WebGL2 backend — textured pipeline

- `packages/rendering/src/webgl2-backend.ts` — extend `IWebGL2Context` with
  the texture subset: `TEXTURE_2D`, `TEXTURE0`, `RGBA`, `UNSIGNED_BYTE`,
  `LINEAR`, `CLAMP_TO_EDGE`, `TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER`, `TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER`,
  `TEXTURE_WRAP_S`, `TEXTURE_WRAP_T`, `createTexture`, `bindTexture`,
  `texImage2D` (source-overload form), `texParameteri`, `activeTexture`,
  `deleteTexture`, `uniform1i`.
- Add a second GLSL program (`FRAGMENT_SHADER_SOURCE_TEXTURED`, sampling
  `texture(u_texture, v_uv)` and multiplying by `u_opacity`; vertex shader
  gains a `v_uv` varying derived from the unit quad, Y-flipped to match
  image/video top-left-origin vs GL bottom-left texture convention).
- Backend keeps a private `Map<AssetId, IGLTexture>`: lazily creates +
  uploads via `texImage2D` on first sight of an asset's `image-source`;
  **re-uploads every frame** when the source is a live `HTMLVideoElement`
  (detect via presence of `videoWidth`/currentTime-style duck check or a
  `kind` tag from the resolver — decide exact detection at implementation
  time), skips re-upload for static images (uploaded once, cached forever).
  `drawNode` picks the textured program + bound texture when
  `node.texture?.kind === "image-source"`, else the existing flat-color
  program.
- Extend `fake-webgl2-context.ts` accordingly.

### 6. WebGPU backend — textured pipeline

- `packages/rendering/src/webgpu-backend.ts` — extend `IGPUDevice`/
  `IGPUQueue` with `createTexture`, `createSampler`, and
  `queue.copyExternalImageToTexture({ source }, { texture }, size)` (the
  idiomatic real WebGPU API for uploading `ImageBitmap`/`HTMLVideoElement`
  sources directly, no manual byte extraction needed).
- Add a second WGSL shader module + render pipeline with a `texture_2d<f32>`
  + `sampler` binding alongside the existing uniform buffer binding.
- Backend keeps a private `Map<AssetId, { texture, bindGroup }>`, same
  lazy-create/re-upload-for-video rule as WebGL2. `drawFrame` selects
  pipeline per node based on `texture` presence.
- Extend `fake-webgpu-context.ts` (or equivalent WebGPU test double)
  accordingly.

  `metadata-extractor.ts`/`thumbnail-generator.ts`:
  - `resolveImageSource(assetId)`: `assetManager.getBytes` →
    `createImageBitmap(new Blob([bytes], { type: entry.mimeType }))`,
    cached forever in a `Map<AssetId, ImageBitmap>` (static content, no
    invalidation needed).
  - `resolveVideoSource(assetId)`: `assetManager.getBytes` → Blob URL →
    persistent `<video>` element (muted, `playsInline`), cached per
    `assetId` in a `Map<AssetId, HTMLVideoElement>`.
  - `resolve(assetId)` (the `ITextureSourceProvider` method): synchronous
    cache read only. On a miss, fires the async resolve in the background
    (fire-and-forget) and returns `undefined` for this frame — the caller
    (backend) falls back to the placeholder color for that frame, and the
    real content appears once decode finishes and the next tick/frame
    redraws. No blocking awaits inside the render loop.
  - `getRawPixels(assetId)`: for the Software backend — lazily draws the
    resolved `image-source` into an offscreen `<canvas>` once and
    `getImageData()`s it into a cached `Uint8ClampedArray`; for video, this
    is a one-shot snapshot (not live per-frame), an accepted scope limit
    since Software is the CI/no-GPU fallback rung, not the interactive path.
  - `getDimensions(assetId)`: synchronous cache read of
    `{width, height}` sourced from the catalog entry (`assetManager.get`),
    resolved via the same background-fetch-then-cache pattern as `resolve`.
  - Video/Playhead sync: play/pause the cached `<video>` element in lockstep
    with `kernel.playback`'s playing state; on scrub/pause, seek
    `currentTime` to the tick's equivalent seconds. Confirm the exact
    play/pause query surface on `kernel.playback` (Scheduler-driven
    Playhead, Phase 5) at implementation time.
- `apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/frame-state-builder.ts` — add an optional
  parameter (e.g. `dimensionsLookup?: (assetId: AssetId) => IBounds | undefined`)
  used for asset-backed layers (Image/Video/Sticker — has `assetId`) in
  place of `PLACEHOLDER_BOUNDS` when a lookup hit exists; falls back to
  `PLACEHOLDER_BOUNDS` otherwise (first-render-before-resolved case, and
  Text/Shape/Group layers which have no `assetId`). Also populate the new
  `assetId` field on `IFrameStateLayer`.
- `apps/studio/src/components/canvas/canvas-panel.tsx` — construct one
  `TextureSourceResolver` per mount (alongside `RenderingEngine`, same
  lifecycle rationale already documented here: needs the real canvas/DOM),
  pass it into `new RenderingEngine(backend, textureResolver)` and into
  `buildFrameState(..., (assetId) => textureResolver.getDimensions(assetId))`.
  Update the component's doc comment (currently states "Content is
  placeholder colored rects... no decoder pipeline exists") to reflect the
  new reality.

### 8. Docs

Per this repo's docs workflow (fill stub docs as each engine is built),
replace the "not implemented yet" placeholder-content language with what
was actually built in: `docs/05-rendering-engine/scene-graph.md`,
`canvas-fallback.md`, `webgl.md`, `webgpu.md`, `renderer-overview.md`.

silently leaving it stale.

  `pnpm --filter @motion-studio/studio typecheck/lint/test` after each stage.
- Extend each backend's existing test suite with a texture-branch case using
  the fakes (inject a fake `image-source`/`raw-rgba` texture on a node,
  assert `drawImage`/texture-upload calls happen instead of the
  placeholder-color path).

  unavailable in Node/vitest without heavy polyfilling — following the
  existing precedent (`metadata-extractor.ts`/`thumbnail-generator.ts` have
  no unit tests either), this is verified manually in-browser, not unit
  tested.
- Manual verification (per this project's convention — the user checks UI
  changes themselves): restart the `apps/studio` dev server on port 3000,
  import a real image and a real video asset, drag each onto the Timeline,

# Real texture content for Image/Video layers (Canvas panel)

## Context

The user reported that dropping an image/video onto the Canvas panel shows
only a small flat-colored square in the top-left corner instead of the
actual pixel content. Investigation confirmed this is not a wiring bug — no
render backend has ever drawn real pixel content. Every layer, regardless of
type, draws a `placeholderColor(layerId)` flat rect
(`packages/rendering/src/placeholder-color.ts`), and every layer's bounds
are hardcoded to a `200×200` placeholder box
(`apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/frame-state-builder.ts:24`) because no asset
dimension is tracked anywhere. This was an explicitly documented, deferred
gap (PLAN.md §15.2, §7), not previously implemented.

User chose the full-scope fix: wire real decoded image/video content into
**all four** render backends (WebGPU, WebGL2, Canvas2D, Software), and fix
layer bounds to reflect the asset's real dimensions instead of the
placeholder box. This is genuinely greenfield — no design doc or existing
decode-to-texture path exists to extend.

**Key existing patterns being reused, not reinvented:**
- Browser-only decode already exists twice for one-shot use:
  `apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/metadata-extractor.ts` (`createImageBitmap`
  for images, `<video>` + `onloadedmetadata` for video) and
  `thumbnail-generator.ts` (`<video>` + seek + `drawImage` to a canvas). The
  new resolver mirrors these same browser APIs, just kept alive instead of
  one-shot.
- `AssetManager` already composes `catalog.get` + `blobStore.get` internally
  for `delete()` — the new `getBytes` method follows the same shape.
- Every backend already hand-rolls a minimal DOM/GPU interface
  (`ICanvas2DContext`, `IWebGL2Context`, `IGPUDevice`) so tests can inject
  fakes — texture support extends these same interfaces rather than
  introducing a new abstraction.
- `packages/rendering` stays DOM-decode-free: `RenderingEngine` accepts an
  **injected** `ITextureSourceProvider`; the actual `createImageBitmap`/
  `<video>` decode logic lives in `apps/studio` (app layer owns DOM glue,
  same split as `metadata-extractor.ts`/`thumbnail-generator.ts` today).

**Explicitly out of scope** (flagged, not solved by this change):
- Text/Shape/Group layers keep `PLACEHOLDER_BOUNDS` — modeling their
  intrinsic size is a separate, already-flagged open item.
- Frame-exact video/tick sync — video playback drives the `<video>` element
  natively (play/pause in lockstep with the Playhead); scrubbing seeks it.
  This is an approximation, consistent with CLAUDE.md's already-open "Audio
  clock drift" hard risk (no resync strategy decided yet) — not solved here,
  not regressed either.

  unbounded for this pass, same accepted-risk posture as `TextureCache`.
